entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Shāh Jalāl Mujarrad Kunyāʾī, popularly known as Shah Jalal, was a celebrated Sufi Saint, conqueror and historical figure of Bengal, who played a pivotal role in the Muslim conquest of Sylhet and the spread of Islam into the region, part of a long history of interactions between the Middle East, Central Asia, and South Asia.

Born in unknown circumstances, Shah Jalal's life was marked by his military campaigns and his efforts to establish Islam in the region, earning him recognition as a key figure in the history of Bengal. His legacy continues to be felt in the modern-day cultural and religious landscape of Bangladesh.

The construction of the Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka, Bangladesh, serves as a testament to his enduring impact on the region.
